A tuple for Verilog

You will learn

Which tuple types the Verilog backend lowers, decided from their text alone.

The Verilog backend lowers a tuple type only when its text is plain parentheses with no named field. is_simple_tuple_type checks that the text starts with an opening bracket, ends with a closing one, contains no colon and is not empty. (u8, u16) passes and (u8, x: u16) does not. The three byte tests are functions of the spec of their own, starts_with, ends_with and bytes_contain, and the page lists their answers beside the verdict. is_icarus_builtin accepts one name, __mul_noop, a helper the backend adds by itself, so it has no definition in the source.

Try it

Add a colon to (u8, u16) and watch the third test. Then ask about __mul_noop.

// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
; specs/compiler/verilog_names.t27 -- the names the Verilog backend decides by text alone: the builtins
; Icarus takes without a source-level definition, and the simple tuple type texts its tuple lowering
; accepts.
; --
; The rules live here. `t27c gen-rust` lowers this spec to bootstrap/gen/rust/compiler/verilog_names.rs,
; which bootstrap/src/compiler.rs mounts by #[path] and calls, as it does cse_hoist (#8991) and
; int_type_names (#9093). Never hand-edit the generated copy.
; --
; Provenance: the two bodies are t27o's (specs/tools/t27o/rust_convert.t27) conversion of the hand Rust
; they replace, compiler.rs is_icarus_builtin (a matches! on one name) and is_simple_tuple_type
; (starts_with / ends_with / contains / is_empty on the type text), with these changes, each to existing
; t27 that does the same thing (the char-pattern cases of #9103):
; - t27o compares texts with tri::mutate::plant's same_text, which gen-rust lowers to
;   (&'static str, &'static str) while the parameter here is []const u8; tri::t27b::type_text's `same`
;   has the slice signature (the swap #9093 made).
; - t27o lowers a char pattern of starts_with / ends_with / contains to a text call given the char
;   (#9103 case 1, still open). The prefix is type_text::starts over the same range; the suffix is the
;   byte form (ty.len > 0 and ty[ty.len - 1] == ')'); the contains is rust_std::bytes_contain, the
;   bytes row of t27o's own std table.
; Nothing here is written twice.
; --
; The tests call each function by name. Their expected values are what the hand Rust returned on the
; lab (rustc, the fn text copied verbatim): every arm, and the names each predicate must refuse. t27o's
; own oracle sampled only texts that reach the false arm.
; ASCII only (L3)
; phi^2 + 1/phi^2 = 3 | TRINITY

module VerilogNames;

use tri::t27b::type_text;
use tools::t27o::rust_std;

/// W534: built-in functions that the Verilog backend handles without a source-level definition.
pub fn is_icarus_builtin(name: []const u8) -> bool {
    return type_text::same(name, "__mul_noop");
}

/// Restored from Wave Loop 455 (same botched merge): a tuple type text with no named fields, the only
/// shape the Verilog tuple lowering takes. A colon anywhere (a named field) is refused, and so is every
/// text that is not parenthesised.
pub fn is_simple_tuple_type(ty: []const u8) -> bool {
    return type_text::starts(ty, 0, ty.len, "(") and (ty.len > 0 and ty[ty.len - 1] == ')') and !rust_std::bytes_contain(ty, ':') and !(ty.len == 0);
}

test is_icarus_builtin_answers_one_injected_helper {
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul_noop") == true;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul_noop2") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("_mul_noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("___mul_noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul_noo") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("mul_noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__MUL_NOOP") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin(" __mul_noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul_noop ") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__add_noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul_noopp") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("x__mul_noop") == false;
    assert is_icarus_builtin("__mul_nooq") == false;
}

test is_simple_tuple_type_reads_paren_text_without_fields {
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8, u16)") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("()") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("( )") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8,u16,u32)") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(x)") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("((u8))") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8, (u16, u32))") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("( u8 , u16 )") == true;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(a: u8)") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(:)") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8:u16)") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8, a: u16)") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("u8)") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("u8") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type(")") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type(" [u8] ") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("x(u8)") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("(u8)x") == false;
    assert is_simple_tuple_type("&(u8, u16)") == false;
}
